concepts.title: How Do We Measure?
concepts.definition: Measuring means comparing with a standard: hand spans and footsteps differ from person to person, so we need fixed units that give the same answer in every hand.
concepts.key_idea: A measurement is only as good as its unit: body measures vary, standard units do not.

concepts.title: Standard Units of Length
concepts.definition: The world measures length in SI units: the metre is the standard unit, with centimetre and millimetre for small lengths and kilometre for great distances, each step a clean multiple of ten.
concepts.key_idea: One agreed unit ends all arguments: a metre in Delhi is a metre anywhere on earth.

concepts.title: Correct Way of Measuring Length
concepts.definition: Good measurement has rules: place the scale along the object, begin at the zero or a clear mark, keep the eye vertically above the reading, and if the scale is broken or worn, subtract the starting reading from the ending reading.
concepts.key_idea: Parallax and offset are the two classic errors: eye straight above the mark, and difference cancels a missing zero.
question_patterns: why must the eye be directly above the scale

an object reads 1.0 cm to 10.4 cm what is its length
why should the scale lie along the object

solution_steps.explain: Note where the object begins on the scale.
Note where the object ends on the scale.
The difference is the length, safe even when the zero is missing.

concepts.title: Describing Position and Types of Motion
concepts.definition: An object's position is stated from a chosen reference point, and motion is change of position with time; motion is classified as rectilinear in a straight line, circular about a fixed centre, rotational about an axis, or periodic, repeating at intervals.
concepts.key_idea: Name the reference point first, then the path: with these two, any motion can be described and classified.
